column1: # OPEN LOOPS -- a log of things that will one day CLOSE.
# Append-only. One row per loop EVENT, not one row per loop: `open`, `close`,
# `supersede`, `note`. The set of open loops is DERIVED by taking the latest
# verb for each id -- so there is no mutable `closed` cell to go stale, which is
# what the first draft of this file got wrong.
# WHY IT EXISTS: four errors of one shape. A forward-looking note was written,
# it fired, and nobody closed it:
#   * articles.md art. 11 warned the Wace receipt would reach Wend before she
#     had seen the letter. TRUE ON DAY 55, FIRED ON DAY 65, quoted as live on
#     DAY 77 -- eleven days late.
#   * npcs.md said of Ancel "Unanswered. He will not sit in the square forever."
#     ANSWERED ON DAY 34 and quoted as live on DAY 77 -- FORTY-THREE DAYS.
#   * CHECKLIST section 11 was headed "day 39" while play stood at day 77, and
#     warned in its own second paragraph that snapshots rot.
#   * "Rowe stays until his foot heals" long after he went south with Halm.
# A warning is the one kind of prose that never LOOKS stale. A stale total looks
# like a number and can be checked against a tool; a stale warning looks like a
# warning. So warnings become rows with a due date and a close-out.
# *** `close` REQUIRES `evidence`, and tools/loops.py refuses without it. ***
# A loop cannot be closed with a flag. Closing means CITING THE THING THAT
# CLOSED IT -- which is precisely the step that was skipped on art. 11. Evidence
# is a pointer: "65:2" (day:seq in interactions), "calendar.md:72", a TSV line.
# WHAT MAY NOT GO IN HERE. The test is: DOES IT HAVE A MOMENT AT WHICH IT STOPS
# BEING TRUE?
#   LOOP          "the wool party back ~83"  "Ancel returns in spring"
#   LOGGED FACT   "Cuddy is frail"  "Perrin refers upward"   -> npcs.md / interactions
#   FINDING       "gifts land badly, work lands"              -> articles.md
# If facts get in here the list grows for ever, the DM stops reading it, and it
# becomes the next CHECKLIST.md.
# Seeded 2026-09-11 by walking CHECKLIST section 11 and every warning box in
# articles.md. That walk WAS the first audit. See dlwork/tooling_plan.md phase 1.

Both readings are physical; they cannot both be the cached rule. Either (10,24,V) is a PIVOTING SLAB rather than a hinged leaf, in which case the rule needs a third row for slabs, or three rows used the weaker method by mistake and the seal was worth less than the log claims. (2) The standing-run question: THE ROAD WILL NOT BEAR WEEKLY TRAFFIC and Osk has known it for years -- three days each way, fortnightly, because weekly runs half empty. (3) The wool: he can NAME THE DOOR cloth goes to in Marchford, which is Wend's own open question from day 77

ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO -- not by anybody's choice but by the road. Halm asked once and never again: 'one load's a load. What I'd want is a RUN.' Wend's condition was a load both ways. OSK, who has carried Wethersby-Marchford every fortnight for years, says the route will not bear weekly traffic and that is why there is one carrier on it and not three. Neither Halm nor Wend could have known that; nobody had ever asked the man who did. HALM STILL HAS NO RUN, and that is now a fact about the road rather than an open question

THE CART-HIRE AGREEMENT, one side of one sheet: Osk's customers carried in the party's carts at A FLAT RATE THE LOAD, HIS NAME ON THE CONTRACT WITH HIS CUSTOMER, and the loss his. Wend's alternative to the partnership she refused. *** IT IS NOT AGREED YET -- Osk has not answered. *** Her own framing of the question to put to him: 'whether he'd rather have the run and the risk, or no run at all.' Wend to draft and settle it; the party confirms and does not relay

TWO CARTS OF EMPTY GOING SOUTH. Wend costed the southern list against the CARTS as instructed and it fills about ONE AND A HALF of three -- the dear things are light and the heavy things are cheap. She now has a reason to leave them empty rather than fill them badly, having refused the partnership that would have filled them. UNRESOLVED: what, if anything, the party puts in them. Candidates: the forty jars for Trebb, the narrow cloth once Osk's Marchford name is followed up, or Osk's freight if he takes the flat-rate terms

THE LIST IS COSTED (83:2) -- that half of this loop is done. What remains: Toller's correspondents, the forty jars, and 'who buys narrow cloth in Marchford and at what', which OSK CAN NOW ANSWER WITH A NAME. And the carts leave after today
HOME on the day it was forecast, ten days out. 36 tods at the published 8 gp floor, 288 gp paid. All five back. Hask held the price and made unasked-for arrangements for next season

*** THE WOOL VENTURE'S PURSE IS NOT IN ANY LOG. *** The buying party went out on day 73 with money and came home on the 83rd having paid 288 gp to holders, and NOTHING records where that money came from, what they carried, or what came back. campaign/money.tsv is the PARTY'S purse and this is plainly VENTURE money -- Wend's book, not Dave's -- so it may legitimately sit outside it. But NOTHING SAYS SO, which means the single largest sum moved this month is untracked by design or by accident and nobody can tell which. Either the venture's book becomes a log the way the party's purse did, or money.tsv gets an explicit note saying what it deliberately excludes and why. THE ART.7 EXPOSURE TURNS ON THIS: the cap is 500 gp a season and 288 has just been spent against it

HASK MADE ARRANGEMENTS FOR NEXT SEASON, unprompted, with holders who have not sheared yet -- on a buying trip where his only job was to hold the price. NOBODY HAS SEEN THE TERMS. He is a fighter with CHA 8 who was a bandit a fortnight before this, and he has just committed the venture to something forward. It may be the best thing anybody has done for the wool operation or it may be a promise the venture cannot keep at a rate it did not set. ASK HIM WHAT HE AGREED, and get it to Wend before it is a surprise

SOLVED, and smaller than proposed. The player's ruling: TRACK THE CAP, NOT THE BOOK -- Wend's ledger is hers and is REPORTED, NOT INSPECTED. So money.tsv gained a  column (blank/party = the purse, art7 = the wool venture's 500 gp seasonal commitment), the 288 gp is logged against it, and  computes the exposure. 288 of 500 spent, 212 remaining, and it is in brief.py so it cannot be forgotten. A NON-PARTY ROW CANNOT MOVE THE PURSE and four tests pin that, including one that caught the in/out breakdown failing to reconcile with its own headline the moment a second book existed

HANDLED BY WEND, not the party. Hask could not remember whether he said 'eight' or 'at least eight' and admitted it. Wend is writing to all four holders to ask WHAT THEY UNDERSTOOD, and whatever they answer becomes the terms -- four holders who trust the board are worth more than winning an argument in June. She left the buying with him and said nothing further. THE FORWARD ARRANGEMENTS THEMSELVES ARE SOUND: art.7's term is one season 'reviewed BEFORE shearing' precisely because a man decides whether to shear on what he thinks he will get, so giving four men a number in September is what the clause is FOR

FOUR LETTERS OUT to the holders Hask spoke to, asking WHAT THEY UNDERSTOOD about next season's price. Whatever they answer becomes the terms. Wend's own reasoning: four holders who trust the board are worth more than winning an argument in June. *** THE ANSWERS WILL COME BACK BEFORE SHEARING AND THEY SET THE FORWARD RATE *** -- and art.7's cap is 500 a season with 288 already spent this one

THE TRIP IS A PARTY EXPEDITION, settled. It goes for the FORTY JARS, which are party salvage, and carries Wend's list as freight. SEVEN GO -- Dave, Yrtone, Tristle, Frython, Ista, Blartho and HASK, who asked to and whom Wend does not need this fortnight. Torsat (to 87) and Dellie (to ~88) stay. *** THE NARROW CLOTH, OSK'S MARCHFORD NAME, THE LOOM'S REED AND HEDDLES AND BERN ARE ALL WEND'S *** and were explicitly handed back to her by the player -- the party carries her list, it does not transact her business. Leaves the 84th; Marchford is 3 days each way

*** THE PARTY IS IN TWO PLACES AND CANNOT SEND WORD. *** Dave and Frython ride for Wraye (~5 days each way at 60 mi/day on roads); Yrtone, Tristle, Ista, Blartho and Hask take three carts to Marchford (3 days) with Tam. THEY ARE OUT OF CONTACT FOR ABOUT A WEEK AND THERE IS NO ARRANGED RENDEZVOUS OR DEADLINE -- nobody said where or when they meet again, or what either half does if the other is late. The caravan's business at Marchford is a few days; Dave and Frython's is ten. FIX THIS BEFORE IT MATTERS

DAVE AND FRYTHON CARRY TOLLER'S SIX-CORRESPONDENTS COMMISSION on the Wraye ride. Marchford, Ludbury and Wraye are three TOWNS -- Lyde was considered and rejected, correctly: it is a VILLAGE a day off the road each way, and Toller's condition was 'six correspondents in six TOWNS' because 'two dealers in one town who know each other is one price'. A village has one of a thing or none

RENDEZVOUS SET, and it is the sensible one: *** THEY MEET BACK IN WETHERSBY *** unless they happen to fall in with each other on the road. No deadline, no waiting anywhere, no half sitting in Marchford wondering. Each half does its business and comes home. The riders are the longer trip by about a week

NO PLACE ID FOR THE ROADS THEMSELVES. Scenes happen on the north road constantly -- Osk on day 6, Pell on day 58 and again on day 84 -- and every one is filed at the nearest named landmark with the real position buried in the summary. log.py correctly REFUSED 'road_south' because it is not in places.tsv. The roads ARE data (campaign/roads.tsv, built 2026-09-12), so either scenes learn to cite a road plus a distance along it, or a few milestones become places. Low priority; it costs nothing today and it loses precision every time

TWO OF SIX, IN ONE MORNING. Ossery the Marchford mercer took the arrangement at once (d6=5, reaction 44) -- Toller's six-in-six-towns is a description of the trade Ossery is already in. AND HE NAMED THREE MORE DEALERS IN OTHER TOWNS (d6=2, d3=3), unasked. *** THE MECHANISM IS THAT TOLLER'S OWN CONDITION MAKES THE NETWORK SELF-BUILDING: 'two dealers in one town who know each other is one price' means the dealers must NOT be in one town -- and a man who buys to sell on has no reason to protect a rival fifty miles away and every reason to want more places to sell on to. *** So: Toller (Wethersby), Ossery (Marchford), and three names to try at Ludbury and Wraye

THREE OF SIX. Ossery's three Ludbury names all refused the goods pitch and ONE TOOK THE REFRAME: not 'we have things to sell' but 'WE ARE A ROUTE INTO A DISTRICT YOU DO NOT REACH'. *** AND HE WANTS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT WAS ASSUMED: NOT TO BUY FROM DRAYCOT BUT TO SELL INTO IT -- access to SIR AYMER'S HALL, which is a NAME and not a good. *** The party holds exactly that currency and did not know it: the licence, Ottir's surety, Wace's own receipt, Cuddy. THE LESSON FOR THE REMAINING THREE: stop offering goods. Offer the route

THE RING: identification is a SPELLCASTER, not a shop, and THE COST IS THE MATERIAL COMPONENT -- a pearl of not less than 100 gp, consumed per casting, one property per segment of the caster's level (rules/spells-1st-level.md). So the question at Wraye is WHO CASTS IT AND WHOSE PEARL. *** AND FRYTHON IS A MAGIC-USER *** -- identify is 1st level, he does not have it, but a library that HOLDS the spell and a magic-user who could COPY it is a different transaction from a stranger asking a favour. The library wants an INTRODUCTION, not coin, and the party knows nobody within 146 miles of it

CORRECTION: 'Nobody in Ludbury can identify the ring' was established on DAYS 25-27, not today -- calendar.md says so in plain words and the DM had forgotten it. Today added only the REASON: the city's one magic-user is retained by the church, and pearls are one supplier's order-book rather than stock. Wraye stands as the lead, now with a cause behind it rather than a rumour

*** NEOT'S PEARL, AND WHAT IS OWED FOR IT. *** He gave the party his own hundred-gold pearl -- bought years ago, his and not the church's -- and REFUSED MONEY. The price is that HE IS TO BE TOLD WHAT THE RING TURNS OUT TO BE. It cannot be discharged at a counter, it cannot be paid by anybody else, and it requires somebody to come back to Ludbury or to write. *** IF THE RING IS NEVER IDENTIFIED THE DEBT STILL STANDS *** -- he is owed the answer, including the answer 'we still do not know'. A man who takes no outside work and refused coin has asked for one thing

DAVE PROMISED MORE THAN WAS ASKED, unprompted: 'We'll come back THROUGH and tell you, and we'll give you THE STORY OF HOW WE GOT IT too.' Neot asked only to be told what the ring is. Dave has bound the party to (a) coming back through Ludbury in person rather than writing, and (b) telling a man retained in one room for eleven years where it came from -- which means Quasqueton, the dais in area 27, and a dead wizard's stronghold. HE ASKED FOR AN ANSWER AND HAS BEEN PROMISED AN ADVENTURE

SOLD TO TREBB, 7 gp the lot, at his own figure. The loop opened on day 71 when Toller handed them off entirely -- 'forty of anything isn't curio, it's STOCK' -- and he was right about all of it: they were stock, they were worth almost nothing, and the dyer was the man. B1's own text calls them 'of no particular value' and 27 of the 40 turned out to be a dyer's mordants and colourants. *** THE PARTY DID NOT SHOP THE TANNER TREBB HAD JUST NAMED THEM ***

*** A LUDBURY MAN IS TELLING HOLDINGS ON THE SOUTHERN ROAD THAT THE PARTY'S AT-COST PRICES ARE NOT REALLY AT COST. *** Reached FENN, a partner, and cooled him to 14. THE ACCUSATION IS TRUE AND THE PARTY FOUND IT FIRST -- Wend, day 77: carriage follows WEIGHT, the iron was 14% of the Ludbury load's value and 51% of its weight, 'at cost' ran 50-70 gp BELOW cost. L024 is already open to fix it forward. BUT NOBODY OUTSIDE WETHERSBY KNOWS THAT, and a true thing said by a stranger beats a true thing you have not said. UNRESOLVED: who is saying it and why, and whether the answer is to publish the corrected costing or to find the man

*** FENN'S 90 GP IS NOW A COIN DEBT, NOT A FIBRE DEBT -- and it was changed in his yard by one party member without Wend. *** Yrtone offered it to simplify a conversation that had got away from her, and Fenn took it AND WAS QUIETLY DISMAYED (d6=1): he chose fibre on day 27 on purpose, because a man with land and no coin would rather owe what he grows, and coin now means he must SELL the crop himself for cash in a district where the party is the only reliable buyer. THREE THINGS FELL OUT UNDISCUSSED: (1) WEND PUT IN 5 GP ON THE SAME BUY-BACK TERMS AND SAID 'I WANT THE FIBRE, NOT THE FRACTION' -- she is not here and has not agreed; (2) the party's cloth chain loses its only flax input; (3) the day-60 question of WHOSE MAN DILL IS is now moot in the wrong direction. THIS NEEDS PUTTING TO WEND BEFORE IT IS FINAL, and it is the party's own money so it IS theirs to change -- but hers is in it too

*** THE PARTY'S POSITION, GIVEN OUT OF GAME AND STANDING. *** (1) WEND IS MADE WHOLE: her 5 gp back plus 1 gp on top, 6 in total, as interest. Not a refund -- a return with something for the use of it. (2) THE PARTY IS NOT WITHDRAWING FROM FLAX, ONLY FROM NEGOTIATING IT: there are other growers, and if Wend wants to go on buying from Fenn SHE MAY, with the party's blessing and no opposition. (3) THE REASON IS NOT THE MONEY: 'we're just not going to stand around trying to argue and negotiate something we know nothing about.' Yrtone spent a morning being corrected on retting by the man she came to help. *** SO THE COIN TERMS ARE NOT A RETREAT FROM FENN. THEY ARE THE PARTY GETTING OUT FROM BETWEEN WEND AND A TRADE SHE UNDERSTANDS AND THEY DO NOT *** -- which is the same move they made with Osk on day 80 and the same one they made when they handed her the venture entirely
